children: Nomura maintained its 'Buy' rating on TVS Motor following the appointment of Peyman Kargar as Director & CEO, effective January 27, 2027. Kargar will succeed K N Radhakrishnan (KNR), who will continue as CEO until then and subsequently serve as a Non-Executive Director until the AGM in July 2027.

KNR joined TVS Motor in 2004, became President in 2008 and Director & CEO in 2018. During his tenure, TVS delivered revenue and PAT CAGRs of 16% and 30%, respectively, while its market capitalisation rose from Rs 8.3 billion in FY08 to Rs 2.05 trillion as of August 28, 2026.

Kargar joined TVS in April 2025 as President, International Business, and brings more than 30 years of global automotive experience across Europe, Asia and the Middle East. Before joining TVS, he was Global Chairman & President of Infiniti, Nissan's luxury brand. He has also held senior roles at Nissan and Datsun, including overseeing Nissan's Africa, Middle East & India operations and Datsun across more than 80 countries.
Nomura noted that TVS' 2W/3W exports grew 31%/50% in FY26, while exports' share of total volumes increased to 26.9% from 25.2% in FY25.

"We believe expansion into premium and global segment portfolios will gain greater focus under the new CEO, given his experience across luxury and global markets," Nomura said. "With Norton's imminent launch, execution in the premium segment will be a key monitorable."

While the leadership change could lead to "some near-term increase in perceived risk", Nomura said it continued to maintain its positive stance, given the strong demand outlook and success of new products. The brokerage expects TVS to deliver 9%/13% volume/revenue CAGRs over FY27F-29F.
Nomura estimates TVS volumes will grow 16%/10%/8% and EBITDA margins will be 13.1%/14.3%/14.2% over FY27-29F. "We expect margins to expand due to INR weakness, price hikes and operating leverage."
The brokerage values TVS at 33x average FY28F-29F EPS to derive a target price of Rs 4,594. The stock currently trades at 32.6x FY28 EPS.

title: Nomura retains 'Buy' on TVS Motor; sees greater focus on premium, global markets under new CEO
